name: SC-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Sheri Biggs running with large fundraising edge
Minimal Democratic funding and no independent polls
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~95%
model.rationale: The R+21 lean, Biggs's incumbency and roughly twelve-to-one fundraising advantage leave Lehmacher with no visible path, and markets price her win at only about 4%. The forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin with slightly reduced uncertainty given the one-sided evidence.
model.watch: A major outside-spending surge for the Democrat or a scandal involving Biggs would be the only realistic route to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 3rd District is deeply Republican territory, and first-term incumbent Sheri Biggs is seeking re-election with the advantages that status brings. She has raised over $500,000 and holds more than $218,000 on hand, while Democrat Eunice Lehmacher has raised about $41,000 with under $18,000 available. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot but lacks any reported fundraising.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's R+21 baseline, the fundraising gap, and prediction markets that give the Republican roughly a 95% chance. The expected margin is near nineteen points Republican, with the seat rated Safe R.
